summary: This bill requires the Environmental Protection Agency to concurrently publish implementation regulations and guidance when establishing or revising national ambient air quality standards, and it specifies that the 2024 particulate matter standard will not apply to certain preconstruction permit applications if specific conditions related to application completeness or public notice are met.

scores.thoughts: This bill aims to streamline the implementation of national ambient air quality standards by requiring the EPA to concurrently publish regulations and guidance with any new or revised standard. It also delays the applicability of the 2024 Primary Annual Particulate Matter 2.5 Standard to certain preconstruction permits if specific conditions are met. While it includes provisions to ensure best available control technology and lowest achievable emission rate technology are still required, and allows states to impose more stringent requirements, the primary effect of delaying the application of new air quality standards to permits could lead to a temporary reduction in environmental protection by slowing the adoption of stricter pollution controls for new or modified stationary sources.
